issues.description: Default turn_detection_mode silently changed from EXTERNAL to FIXED is a breaking behavior change
issues.detail: Flipping the default from EXTERNAL to FIXED silently changes endpointing semantics for every existing caller who relied on the default. Existing pipelines that emitted UserStoppedSpeakingFrame for finalization will no longer trigger it. The changelog labels this as a fix rather than a breaking default change, with no deprecation path or migration notes. Either preserve EXTERNAL as default, make the parameter required, or mark this as a breaking version bump with explicit migration guidance.

issues.description: TurnDetectionMode and EndOfUtteranceMode are two parallel enums encoding the same concept with implicit mapping
issues.detail: _enable_vad is computed by checking end_of_utterance_mode against {FIXED, EXTERNAL}, but the public API and changelog describe behavior in terms of turn_detection_mode. Both enums now have FIXED and EXTERNAL members and the mapping between them is implicit and place-oriented. State the invariant explicitly, unify into a single enum, or derive _enable_vad from one source of truth so the two stay in lockstep.

issues.description: Frame-listener narrowing from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame may silently drop finalization
issues.detail: process_frame previously finalized on UserStoppedSpeakingFrame and now finalizes only on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame. If VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame is not a subclass, any pipeline emitting plain UserStoppedSpeakingFrame (manual stops, push-to-talk, scripted tests) will never finalize. The class-hierarchy assumption and intended invariant are not stated. Document the contract explicitly, handle both frame types, or add tests covering both paths.

issues.description: split_sentences tri-state Optional[bool] collapsed to bi-state via 'or False' coercion
issues.detail: params.split_sentences is typed Optional[bool] with default None, then passed as `SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=params.split_sentences or False)`. This conflates 'not specified' (None) with 'explicitly False', destroying any 'use library default' intent. Either type it as `bool = False` and drop the Optional, or only set speech_segment_config when the user explicitly supplied a value. Pick one channel and state the contract.

issues.description: SpeechSegmentConfig is unconditionally overwritten, clobbering any prior config
issues.detail: `config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(...)` is always constructed even when the user passed nothing. This overwrites any speech_segment_config set elsewhere and forces a value when the SDK might have shipped a meaningful default. Either only set the attribute when the user supplied a value, or set just `emit_sentences` on the existing object.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics() call moved without explanation
issues.detail: The `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` line was relocated from after the broadcast/interruption calls to before them, still commented out. Dead code carrying an implicit ordering claim is noise. Either the metric belongs at a specific point and should be uncommented with rationale, or it should be deleted.

issues.description: _prepare_config uses a hand-maintained attribute-name allowlist with hasattr/setattr loop
issues.detail: The list of attribute names with hasattr/setattr is fragile: it loses static checkability, hides which fields the SDK version supports, and split_sentences flows through this loop AND is set explicitly via SpeechSegmentConfig a few lines later. Pick one mechanism — explicit assignments or model-field iteration — so value flow is obvious and version drift is easier to spot.

issues.description: _enable_vad name is misleading after semantics change
issues.detail: After the change, `_enable_vad` no longer means 'VAD is on' — it means 'VAD is on AND we're not in a Pipecat-controlled mode'. The list-membership check should be a tuple/set rather than a fresh list. Rename to something like `_emit_vad_frames` or document the invariant inline so the next maintainer doesn't read it as the obvious thing.

issues.description: Changelog inconsistency: split_sentences listed as 'added', default flip and frame swap mixed under 'fixed'
issues.detail: changelog/3328.added.md mentions only split_sentences while changelog/3328.fixed.md mixes the VAD frame change, the default change to FIXED, and conditional VAD-frame emission. The new TurnDetectionMode.FIXED enum value is arguably an addition, and the default flip is a behavior change, not a fix. The PR description also omits split_sentences entirely. Reclassify entries so readers can tell what is new API surface vs bug fix vs behavior change.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a clear verdict: NEEDS-WORK before merge. The dominant concern is the silent default flip from TurnDetectionMode.EXTERNAL to FIXED — all six reviewers flag this as a breaking behavior change disguised as a fix, with no migration path. Five-to-six reviewers also flag the parallel TurnDetectionMode/EndOfUtteranceMode enums (implicit mapping governing _enable_vad), the narrowed frame-listener from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame (risks silent finalization loss), and the Optional[bool] split_sentences coerced via 'or False' (tri-state collapsed to bi-state). Supporting concerns include unconditional SpeechSegmentConfig overwrite, shuffled commented-out metrics line, misleading _enable_vad name, fragile attribute-allowlist in _prepare_config, and changelog miscategorization. Recommended path: split into separate commits, preserve or explicitly bump the default, state the enum-and-frame-type invariants in the contract, and resolve the dead metrics line.
